about.text: Our Legacy of Quality and Innovation

DuBose Pipe & Gate traces its roots back to 1976 with the establishment of the company by Bill DuBose. In the early years, Bill crafted panels and gates under the shade of a tree, committed to building a brand known for strength, durability, and lasting value. Through hard work, attention to detail, and a deep respect for his customers, Bill earned a reputation people could count on. Upon Bill's passing the company was handed to his son William, who opened a new yard in Lampasas, Texas, in the early 1990s under the name DuBose Pipe & Gate. With the support of his wife, Candy, William continued to grow the business while preserving the same standards of quality and dependability that began with his father. Today, Candy continues to manage the business with a steady hand and a strong commitment to the DuBose name. Under her leadership, DuBose Pipe & Gate remains focused on providing durable panels, gates, pipe, feeders, and livestock solutions built for hardworking ranchers, farmers, and landowners across Texas. The company’s foundation has never changed: build strong products, treat people right, and carry the DuBose legacy forward with pride.

sheep-and-goat-panels.text: Sheep & Goat Panels - Solutions For Your Small Livestock

DuBose Pipe & Gate offers specialized panels for sheep and goats, ensuring your smaller livestock are securely contained. Our custom solutions are built to last, providing peace of mind and exceptional quality. We also offer design and delivery services for all our products.Our sheep and goat panels consist of an upper and lower section. The lower section consists of 4"X4" welded wire. The top section consists of evenly spaced rails. These panels are typically used for sheep, goats, and pigs.
Designed to withstand the rigors of daily use, our durable panels offer the unmatched reliability that is imperative for Central Texas ranchers facing harsh weather and active livestock.
Call Today - We can deliver an excellent setup that will make your containment issues a thing of the past!
